newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South Africa turns corner on debt - deputy finmin.
newsitem.headline: South Africa turns corner on debt - deputy finmin.

text.p: South Africa has made progress in getting debt under control, reducing total debt to 55 percent of GDP, Deputy Finance Minister Gill Marcus said on Wednesday.

"Although our deficit is reducing, and with it our borrowing requirements, our interest bill for 1997/98 is estimated to be 39.6 billion rand, or 21.2 percent of the total budget and 6.4 percent of GDP," she said in a speech to parliament.
"But in terms of our total projected debt by March 1998 of just under 342 billion rand, we have begun to turn the corner, reducing it to 55 percent of GDP," Marcus said.
